mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry or notary in the country of origin of the corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for Hague Convention member states; China joined effective 7 November 2023) OR Consular Legalization (for non-Hague members)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / certificate of non-bankruptcy of the corporate founder, issued within 3 months before filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or competent governmental authority in the founder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy and proof of residential address of each UBO and the proposed SAS Président, notarized in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or equivalent public officer in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified translation into French of all above documents by a sworn translator (traducteur assermenté) registered with a French Cour d'appel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Neither apostille nor legalization required for the translation itself; the certified translation is appended to the original apostilled documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, the SAS Président, and any authorized signatories against (i) the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, (ii) United Nations Security Council sanctions, (iii) the French national asset-freezing list (gels d'avoirs published by the Ministry of Economy, administered by Trafin), and (iv) the US OFAC SDN list for USD-denominated clearing risk. Enhanced due diligence is statutorily required for Politically Exposed Persons, their family members, and close associates under Article L. 561-10 of the Code monétaire et financier. Screening must occur pre-incorporation, upon any change in control, and on an ongoing risk-based basis with re-screening at least every 24 hours through a licensed French financial institution or compliance software provider before banking onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) at https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; name availability verified against the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS) via the official databases infogreffe.fr and data.inpi.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the mandatory statutory language pursuant to Loi n° 94-665 du 4 août 1994 (loi Toubon) and Article L. 123-9 of the Code de commerce. The company name (dénomination sociale) must be written in Latin script; a purely foreign-language name is admissible only if it does not conflict with public order, is sufficiently distinctive, and is accompanied by a French translation in the statutes when the name is descriptive of the corporate object. The articles of association and all supporting filings must be submitted in French; any foreign-language document must be translated by a sworn translator.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Preliminary note: French law does not provide a statutory corporate name reservation; the 30-day window corresponds to the practical planning horizon for domain registration and INPI trademark priority. Upon rejection by the Greffe du tribunal de commerce (or by the INPI-administered Guichet unique), the applicant shall: (1) within 15 days of rejection, file a revised set of articles of association under a corrected name through the Guichet unique; (2) if the Greffe maintains the refusal on the ground that the name is identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS name or INPI trademark, the applicant may petition the President of the Tribunal de commerce of the registered-office jurisdiction in summary proceedings (référé) to order registration; (3) an appeal against the juge du fond's decision lies to the Cour d'appel within 15 days of notification; (4) if the conflict involves an INPI trademark, the applicant may file an opposition under Article L. 712-3 of the Code de la propriété intellectuelle or negotiate a coexistence agreement. The rejection does not prohibit the applicant from incorporating under an alternative name and applying to register the contested name as a trademark, provided no prior right is infringed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for an SAS provided the condition of Article L. 123-11-1 and R. 123-167 of the Code de commerce are satisfied: the registered office (siège social) may be established at a commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation holding a prefectural approval) when the company does not yet have its own business premises; the domiciliation contract is strictly time-limited to a maximum of 5 years from registration. For the ISIC 7120 factory inspection and quality-control agency, a virtual office is administratively acceptable for correspondence and legal domiciliation, but the company must retain real operational substance in France: a French bank account, local management (Président), and sufficient records demonstrating actual inspection mandate performance. The DGFiP and URSSAF treat the absence of substantive premises as a red flag and may recharacterize the French establishment as fictitious.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate risk: quantified at 20–25% cumulative probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 3 fiscal years. The risk increases to approximately 30% if (i) the registered office is exclusively a commercial domiciliation address, (ii) the company files low payroll with zero French employees, or (iii) the company derives more than 80% of revenue from foreign group entities. Inspections are conducted by the DGFiP tax audit directorate and by URSSAF for social security substance verification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French avocat (law firm) registered with a bar (Ordre des avocats)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: €2,000–€4,000 for a standard SAS incorporation file; €2,500 used for a standard commercial inspection/QC company

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce, Title II, Book II, Articles L. 227-1 et seq. (Sociétés par actions simplifiées)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) of the Tribunal de Commerce
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de la SAS (Articles of Association)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital requirement of 1 euro, which must be paid up in full upon incorporation; no escrow account required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED by the initial shareholders and proposed directors of the Société par Actions Simplifiée: (1) Subscription to the full share capital of 1,000 euros; (2) Adoption of the registered office at 45 Avenue des Champs-Élysées, 75008 Paris, France; (3) Appointment of Jean Martin as Président, Marie Dubois as Directeur Général, and Pierre Laurent as other officer, with full powers of representation and management; (4) Authorization to file the Articles of Association with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); (5) Grant of powers to the officers to complete all incorporation formalities, including tax and social registrations. Adopted unanimously in accordance with the Code de commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) via guichet-entreprises.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform name search on INPI database to ensure availability; if available, proceed to file incorporation documents with the chosen name. Submit via online portal with required documents.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and legal form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name rejected, select alternative name and resubmit application

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public or direct filing with RCS via GUFIE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a notary to draft the SAS statutes including share capital, object, directors' powers. Sign the act and obtain notary certification. Deposit the original with the RCS.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amendments if queried by RCS, additional filings

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Documents with RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique en Ligne des Formalités des Entreprises (GUFIE) at guichet-entreprises.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload scanned signed Articles of Association, proof of payment (none), director details, and other mandatory forms. Receive SIREN number immediately upon successful filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rejection and resubmission within 15 days with corrections

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining SIREN, SIRET, and Tax Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GUFIE portal and French tax authorities (URSSAF, INSEE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the SIREN to register for social security, VAT if applicable, and open corporate bank account. Complete all post-incorporation declarations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Follow-up with authorities for delayed processing

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Setup and Officer Appointments

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene first board meeting to appoint officers, adopt internal rules, and update filings if necessary. Ensure compliance with governance requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration as a commercial inspection and testing agency

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A - Pre-shipment inspection activities do not involve manufacturing, wastewater, VOCs, or hazardous waste handling

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique; online portal: impots.gouv.fr; single-window business formalities: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises, operated by INPI, at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; customs and excise authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI), douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French-established SAS: incorporate via the INPI Guichet unique; INSEE automatically issues SIREN/SIRET, and the DGFiP service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) opens the corporate tax account and allocates the intra-Community VAT number (format 'FR' + 2-digit key + SIREN) without a separate application. The President must ensure the activity declaration and beneficial-ownership data are filed, and thereafter file monthly or quarterly VAT returns and annual corporate income tax returns (liasse fiscale) through impots.gouv.fr. For a non-resident entity without a French fixed establishment: file CERFA n° 15798*01 with the DGFiP 'unité des non-résidents' (Montreuil) for French VAT registration; non-EU businesses generally must appoint an accredited tax representative (représentant fiscal) unless a waiver applies; alternatively, non-established sellers of imported goods may register under IOSS, and EU distance sellers under OSS (with the €10,000 annual distance-sales threshold applying for intra-EU supplies).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a French SAS is a corporation subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at entity level on profits derived from enterprises operated in France under the territoriality rule of CGI art. 209; it is not eligible for pass-through taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: French law has no US-style check-the-box election; classification follows legal form and substance. Available elections and mechanisms: (i) fiscal integration (intégration fiscale, CGI art. 223 A) for a French parent holding at least 95% of eligible French subsidiaries; (ii) single VAT taxable person grouping (assujetti unique, CGI art. 256 C quater, effective from 2023) for financially, economically and organisationally integrated French entities; (iii) option to waive the small-business VAT exemption franchise (CGI art. 293 B) in order to invoice VAT to B2B clients; (iv) French hybrid-mismatch rules transposing ATAD (CGI arts. 209 B and 212 bis) neutralising deduction/non-inclusion and double-deduction outcomes; (v) option for the simplified VAT payment scheme and payment-basis VAT accounting where eligible (CGI art. 269-2-c).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Euro operates under full capital and current account convertibility per EU and French FX liberalization. Profit remittances and service fee receipts face no convertibility barriers for EU-resident or qualifying non-resident entities. Hurdles limited to standard tax withholding (e.g., 12.8% on dividends) and beneficial ownership verification; no capital controls apply to routine corporate inflows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export-related receipts required under French law. Receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts or converted at spot rates per commercial contract terms. Voluntary surrender facilities available through Banque de France for statistical purposes only.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for cross-border liquidity via regulated EMI providers such as Wise and Revolut Business. Legal constraints confined to French AML/CFT obligations, TRACFIN reporting, and e-CBI tax filing; no prohibition on offshore digital EMIs for EU-established SAS entities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding fully permitted for French SAS entities using video KYC, e-signature, and biometric verification. Physical presence of directors or shareholders required only for enhanced due diligence cases or non-resident beneficial owners exceeding 25% stake.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent beneficial ownership or source of funds from high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ultimate beneficial owner declarations, passport copies, corporate chart, bank reference letters, and proof of legitimate inspection service revenue
Country risk assessment, PEP screening certificate, and senior management attestation

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Instant with purpose code 900 for capital contributions. Verification requires French SIREN/SIRET confirmation, beneficial ownership proof, and tax ID linkage. Non-resident equity injections cleared through correspondent banks with full KYC/AML documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements cleared via SWIFT MT103 or commercial letters of credit (LC) for supplier or sub-contractor payments. Trade settlements use standard correspondent banking rails; no FX surrender obligations apply to service fee outflows.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No filing authority; approval by the SAS shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A court may order the president to convene shareholders or appoint an agent; late approval alone does not trigger automatic strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit and, where applicable, management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry (Greffe) maintaining the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The president may be ordered to file, potentially subject to a daily penalty; failure to deposit is generally punishable by a fine of up to EUR 1,500, or EUR 3,000 for repeat offences. No automatic strike-off period applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and appendices)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after financial year-end; for a calendar-year close, by the second working day after 1 May, subject to the applicable electronic filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment may incur 0.2% monthly interest and a 5% late-payment surcharge; late or missing returns may incur a 10% surcharge, rising in specified circumstances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual CFE (Cotisation foncière des entreprises) payment, if due
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual balance generally due by 15 December; instalments may apply depending on the prior-year liability
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment may incur a 5% surcharge and 0.2% monthly interest. The amount is assessed according to the business and local tax base; it is not a fixed renewal fee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner information update, if details change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry / INPI through the applicable business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after a change in reportable beneficial-owner information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain accurate information can result in criminal and financial penalties for the company and responsible individuals; no annual confirmation filing is required.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SAS generally must appoint a statutory auditor if it exceeds at least two of these three thresholds at financial year-end: EUR 5 million total assets, EUR 10 million net turnover, or 50 average employees. Separate appointment rules apply to certain groups and controlled entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the Plan Comptable Général; IFRS is not generally required for an unlisted SAS's statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no general annual UBO confirmation. File an update within 30 days when reportable beneficial-owner information changes. Record share transfers and maintain current shareholder information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of share transfers and shareholder accounts, where applicable to the share form

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 300–1,200 annually, depending on provider and services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 5,000–15,000 annually for a small SAS subject to statutory audit; scope and complexity may materially increase fees

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million; at least 75% held by individuals or compatible small entities). Research tax credit (CIR) equal to 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above; Innovation tax credit (CII) equal to 20% of eligible innovation expenses up to EUR 400,000; reduced income rate of 10% for qualified industrial and intellectual property rights under the patent box regime.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_regime: France does not impose a five-year limit. Tax losses under CGI article 209 may be carried forward indefinitely without time limit, but each subsequent taxable year can utilise a maximum of EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable income exceeding EUR 1 million. A one-year carryback is available, capped at EUR 1 million.
corporate_income_tax_regime.entity_level_tax_designation: SAS is taxed at entity level under French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 2065-SD (corporate income tax return) with the 2050/2051 annex series, filed electronically through the professional taxpayer portal at impots.gouv.fr using EDI-TDFC or EFI. Supplementary filing of the annual tax balance (liasse fiscale 2050-series), the optional simplified CbCR form, and VAT returns (CA3) is coordinated through the same e-filing channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return. Four quarterly advance instalments are required on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, with the final settlement included in the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a SAS closing accounts on 31 December, the annual return is due by the second business day following 1 May. For a fiscal year ending at another date, the return is due within three months of the fiscal year-end. Electronic filing is mandatory for all French corporate taxpayers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique French company identification number; nine-digit SIREN followed by five-digit NIC for the registered office of the SAS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the French SAS identification number. Foreign parent company identification is not inserted in this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the SAS and its legal form code. The form shown for a simplified joint-stock company is 'SAS'.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the official name registered with the French Commercial and Companies Register (RCS). If the entity is treated as a French resident entity, no non-resident notation is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address in France. This address determines the territorial jurisdiction of the tax office (SIE) and is used for all formal notices.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned SAS must maintain an effective routing address in France; a simple care-of address may trigger substance review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Intra-EU VAT identification number, normally represented as 'FR' plus 11 digits, issued by INSEE after registration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Required for cross-border service invoicing of inspection fees. The number must be shown on invoices issued to EU clients.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year opening and closing dates. Standard is 01/01 to 31/12 for a calendar-year SAS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not alter the French fiscal year. The fiscal year must be closed in accordance with French accounting rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover excluding VAT, i.e. aggregate inspection, testing, and quality-control fees billed to clients, after excluding value-added tax and any statutory pass-through costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All France-source revenue and export-related inspection revenue performed from France must be reported. Revenue generated by an on-site factory inspection abroad is still taxable if such services are designed, invoiced, and economically managed in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting income before tax taken from the 2050 balance sheet. This includes operating profit of the QC agency and all other ordinary income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For related-party transactions, the corresponding expenses and income lines must be supported by TP documentation in the annexes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adding back non-deductible expenses, adjusting foreign exchange, deducting research credits, loss carryforwards, and applying transfer pricing corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The tax inspector expects the foreign parent's charges, management fees, and royalties to have been deducted strictly under Article 57 CGI and TP rules. Any undocumented related-party deduction should not be included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre 10 - Répartition des bénéfices / bénéficiaires effectifs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed shareholding and beneficial ownership of the SAS, including foreign corporate shareholders and ultimate natural persons.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must be listed with country of tax residence. If treaty relief on distributions is intended, attach a current Form 5000 certificate and relevant tax residency certificate before distribution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge of the tax due under CGI article 1728 plus 0.20% monthly late-payment interest (2.4% annually). A return filed after a formal demand is penalised at 40% for deliberate failure or 80% for fraud or abuse of law. Additional assessment and criminal sanctions may follow the same factual basis.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_context: French-source dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders are subject to withholding tax at 25% under CGI article 119 bis. Payments to non-resident individuals are ordinarily subject to the 30% single flat levy (12.8% income tax plus 17.2% social contributions), subject to treaty reduction and exception.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive reduced rate, the beneficial owner must deliver prior to payment: a certificate of fiscal residence on official Form 5000 completed and stamped by the shareholder's tax authority; the shareholder's annual Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) evidencing effective tax residence in the treaty state; and a statement using Form 5001 / 5002 confirming that the shareholder is the beneficial owner and that it satisfies the shareholding and holding-period conditions (for EU directive relief, generally a minimum 5% or 25% direct shareholding and a two-year holding commitment). The forms must be filed with the paying agent or the relevant French SIE. Where the documentation is incomplete, the paying agent must withhold at the statutory 25% rate and restitution may only be obtained through a claim for overpayment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic withholding tax for payments to non-residents without a French permanent establishment is 33.33% under CGI article 182 B. Under most French tax treaties, royalties are reduced to 0% or 5%; the EU Interest-Royalty Directive secures 0% for qualifying associated enterprises subject to ownership thresholds and actual beneficial ownership. Interest: ordinary commercial and bank trade debt interest paid to non-resident corporate creditors is generally exempt from domestic French withholding tax; specific levies may apply to bond interest. Treaty rates are typically 0% to 10% depending on the treaty partner.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.economic_substance_requirement_for_treat: The shareholder must have real economic substance, actual power to dispose of dividends, and a legitimate business purpose in the residence state. Absent these elements, the French tax administration will deny treaty benefits under OECD principal purpose test jurisprudence and the French abuse-of-right doctrine.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000. Mandatory French Local File and Master File obligations arise where the French entity's annual turnover or balance-sheet total reaches EUR 400 million, or where a controlling or controlled foreign entity has annual turnover or balance-sheet total of EUR 400 million or more. Country-by-Country Reporting mandatory at EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations. Instead, French tax law requires genuine substance for entity-level tax benefits through LPF article L64 (abus de droit), Article 57 CGI controlled-entity rules, and OECD/EU beneficial-ownership requirements. For the QC and pre-shipment inspection sector, a SAS must demonstrate physical premises, qualified employees, performance of actual inspection protocols, insurance coverage, decision-making power in France, and bank accounts with a transparent business purpose. Shell entities cannot obtain treaty relief or retain deductibility of intercompany charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Billing clients for inspection and testing services that were never performed; knowingly declaring a lower taxable profit in Cadre 8 of Form 2065-SD; using undisclosed offshore bank accounts to receive inspection fees through Wise or wire transfers; falsifying the 2050 annexes; manufacturing vendor expenses from related parties to erase French-source profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CGI article 1741: up to 5 years' imprisonment and fine of EUR 75,000; aggravated circumstances, such as use of foreign accounts or concealment through an entity organised outside France, increase the maximum sentence to 7 years' imprisonment and EUR 500,000 fine. Administrative penalties of 40%-80% apply, plus monthly late-payment interest at 0.20%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or direct the false return are personally exposed to criminal conviction, imprisonment, travel bans, and disqualification from managing a French company. French courts may pierce the corporate veil in cases of fraudulent concealment, rendering the director civilly liable for restitution of the evaded corporate income tax.
